name: How big can my ADU be in Los Angeles County, and are there height limits I should worry about?

mainEntity.name: How big can my ADU be in Los Angeles County, and are there height limits I should worry about?

acceptedAnswer.text:
In much of Los Angeles County, detached ADUs can be up to **around 1,200 sq ft**, with height often capped between **16–25 feet** depending on location and zoning. Attached ADUs are typically limited by the size and height of the main house.

State rules require local agencies to allow certain minimum sizes, but local ordinances refine the specific limits and where the unit can sit on your lot. Multifamily parcels have additional options and caps.

Key factors:
- Maximum square footage for detached vs attached ADUs
- Height limits, including special allowances near transit
- Setbacks from rear and side property lines, usually at least 4 feet
- Lot coverage and floor area ratio (FAR) limits that may still apply

Before designing, confirm both the maximum size and realistic buildable area on your particular parcel. Your designer should work backward from those constraints to avoid redesigns during plan review.

An ADU‑savvy designer in LA County will typically start your project with a “zoning envelope” study to define your true max size and height.
acceptedAnswer.description: In Los Angeles County, detached ADUs are commonly allowed up to about 1,200 sq ft, with height limits often between 16–25 feet depending on zoning and proximity to transit. Attached ADUs are typically limited by your main house. Always confirm local size, height, setback, and lot coverage rules before locking in a design.
